requirement:
The `{term}` role followed by a backtick-delimited full definition name MUST reference a named definition. In rendered Markdown, the reference MUST display the definition's phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to its anchored declaration, without a badge. The phrase MUST be escaped appropriately for rendering.

Missing targets and targets of another kind MUST be reported. Escaped references and references in Markdown code examples MUST remain literal. A term reference MUST NOT satisfy a requirement citation or a Rust function's requirement-coverage obligation.
rationale: **Verdict:** `requirements.definitions.references` is satisfied. The code that implements it is marked `{impl}`, and the tests cover its obligations. I found a few small gaps, none of which I count against it. **Implementation** - **Role recognition.** `reference_roles` (src/lib.rs) recognises `{term}` followed by a backtick-delimited name and validates the name. - It skips escaped occurrences (`is_escaped`) and Markdown-protected ranges (`protected_ranges`), so escaped references and references in code examples stay literal. - It also protects a term declaration's `:phrase:` option line. - **Rendering.** `replace_references` (src/lib.rs) replaces a `{term}` reference whose target is a Term definition with a plain `phrase`. It does not call `shield_badge` for this case, so there is no badge. - The phrase goes through `terms::escaped_phrase`, which escapes both Markdown-significant characters and HTML. - Missing targets and targets of another kind are left as literal text. - `replace_definitions` emits the anchored declaration, `phrase`, and `DefinitionKind::anchor` builds that anchor id. - `preprocess_book` applies the replacements to all chapters, including detail pages. - **Reporting.** `validate_references` (src/evidence.rs) reports a `{term}` whose target is missing or is not a Term as "term X has no matching named definition". It then `continue`s, so term references never reach the per-definition coverage bookkeeping and never count as requirement evidence. - **Terms never satisfy citations.** - `missing_function_references` (src/rust_coverage.rs) ignores `Term` roles and Term definitions when deciding whether a Rust item is cited. - The example check in `collect_definitions` accepts only `Cite` or `Test` references to Requirements. - `referenced_terms` (src/terms.rs) separates term references for dependency handling. **Tests (tests/definitions.rs)** - `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` checks that a `{term}` pointing at a requirement (`rules.ready`) and a non-existent name (`missing.name`) are both reported. - `phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved` checks the rendered output. - Exactly one hyperlink is produced, with the right relative href and anchor. - The link has no `shields.io` badge. - The phrase `*alpha* & ` is escaped to `*alpha* & <beta>`. - The inline-code, fenced-code and backslash-escaped forms stay literal. - `outline_inputs_capture_terms_without_counting_them_as_citations` checks that a Rust function with only a `{term}` comment still yields "no requirement or example citation". - `definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked` checks that literal and escaped `{term}` references to a missing name produce no error. **Minor gaps, not counted against the requirement** - `collect_references_with_progress`, which collects term references from files, is marked only with `requirements.references.targets` and not with this requirement. It is generic collection; the term-specific rules live in the marked functions. - Nothing tests that a rendered `{term}` pointing at a missing or wrong-kind target stays literal. - `ReferenceKind::color` has a `Term` arm that is never used, because term references take a separate branch.
